correctness.rationale: For finite strict posets, c1 directed refinement records predecessor and successor counts. For a target forest order each predecessor count equals depth; agreement of c2 color histograms forces every depth-d element of any comparator poset to have unique predecessors at each depth 0..d-1. Transitivity then chains these predecessors, recovering the forest property. Inductively c_r(x) determines the entire successor rooted tree if its remaining height <=r: immediate children among successors are exactly those with predecessor count one larger and their c_(r-1) types recursively determine subtrees. At t=max(1,h), histogram of root colors determines all components among strict posets, so C2 rank<=t+1 identifies the target; c_(t+1) additionally encodes ancestor subtree-type paths and thus orbit partition. Explicit height-two seven-vertex forest pair has same rank-one global colors but distinct root/descendant patterns, requiring rank3. Independently checked the six-vertex C2 indistinguishable pair (two three-chains vs arcs 0->3,0->5,1->2,1->4,2->5,3->4), with two vertices in each of three stable classes and a missing transitive arc. Independently enumerated ALL upper-triangular acyclic digraphs of n<=5 (1,2,8,64,1024), partitioned by cross-graph stable directed refinement and compared rooted component isomorphism type for every forest order: no obstruction below six. Topological labeling covers every acyclic graph up to isomorphism; this is an actual finite exhaustive cutoff, not a random experiment.

originality.rationale: Arvind--Kobler--Rattan--Verbitsky’s tree amenability/color-refinement results concern undirected tree cover graphs, whereas the audited binary relation is the entire strict ancestor order; extraction of cover edges needs a third variable. Kiefer--Schweitzer--Selman’s general C2 identification classification concerns unconditional global identification among relational structures; here forest order identification is only relative to strict posets, with an explicit nontransitive C2-equivalent digraph at six points. Thus neither general theorem directly implies the height-specific relative rank bound plus sharp acyclic cutoff. Alternative tree order terminology still presents a literature risk.
residual_risks: Alternative forest-poset or directed-acyclic-tree terminology could conceal an existing height-rank theorem.
Sharp acyclic n<=5 cutoff is computationally certified from all upper triangular DAG presentations and independently repeated, rather than classified by a separate infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Transitive closure can radically change what two-variable counting logic sees, so treating strict forest orders as binary order relations rather than as undirected cover graphs is mathematically substantive. Exact rank t+1 identification, orbit stabilization and the smallest acyclic nontransitive counterexample locate a sharp logical boundary for a natural hereditary poset class. The six-point obstruction is motivated by the necessity of a transitivity promise, not an arbitrary tiny negative example.
